paragraphs: Here's what this little story teaches me, friend. The man lost something that wasn't even his. He cried out, "Oh, my master," and then he said, "it was borrowed!" (2 Kings 6:5). He didn't hide it or pretend nothing happened. He told Elisha, and that is the whole beginning of the miracle.

Look at what Elisha asks him: "Where did it fall?" (2 Kings 6:6). Not a lecture, not a pile of questions about whose fault it was. Then the man of God made the iron float, and the man just reached out his hand and took it (2 Kings 6:6-7). I think this tells us the God who cares about a big prophet's house also cares about one borrowed axe head, and that is GOOD news for your small stuff, baker.

So when you drop something that isn't yours to drop, run to Him, not away from Him. Bring Him the problem, point to the spot where it went wrong, and let Him handle what you can't fix. I spent years thinking my loss was too small for anybody to care about, and I was wrong about that! The One who made iron float sees you, and He is never too busy for your little problem.
